comment: The 2026-08-07 repo/spec audit, in the findings grammar (FR-001). SC-001's corpus and US1's largest fixture. Keys are stable identities: B/T/C/F card numbering from the review artifact is preserved in notes, not keys.

findings.summary: Node coroutines are dispatched fire-and-forget and the reaper never awaits task.result(), so node exceptions vanish; PENDING re-dispatch mints fresh virtual keys for a node whose task may still be alive.
findings.notes: B1. Cheap partial (await task.result() in the reaper) belongs to the bugfix epic; the structural fix is owned by the node-child-workflows epic (T1).

findings.summary: The judge key lease in _verify has no try/finally bracket: a raise between issue and delete leaks the virtual key for its 24h TTL and drops the usage-ledger row for the attempt.
findings.notes: B2. The agent-key path at :1469 is the good example; the recovery path at :1964-2007 shares the gap.

findings.summary: gh CLI calls run via subprocess.run with no timeout on the workflow worker's thread, blocking the event loop against the 5s agent heartbeat and manufacturing false TIMEOUT classifications.
The landing poll's dead branch plus a timeout-less wait_condition can park an epic forever with no escalation when a landing neither merges nor fails cleanly.
findings.notes: B4. Bugfix epic; interacts with the landing long-poll idea (T5).

findings.summary: A Temporal cancel of EpicWorkflow bypasses the kill_epic salvage sequence (no CancelledError handling), so cancellation skips salvage, key cleanup, and evidence recording.
gate_timeout_s and poll_interval_s are read into config but nothing consumes them — dead plumbing that misleads the operator into believing the dials work.

Every node attempt runs inside one EpicWorkflow history (~2 MiB per judged attempt, zero continue-as-new, 50 MB terminate threshold); a child workflow per node bounds history and fixes fire-and-forget structurally.
findings.notes: T1 -> node-child-workflows epic. Cheap partial available first: pass diffs by reference.

findings.summary: All activities share one task queue though worktrees and stores are host-local; host-affinity queues (workgraph-<hostname>, asserted via activity.info().task_queue) are the Temporal-native fix, and 001's usage-ledger queue was never implemented.
The Telegram bridge process is unsupervised: its death silently converts every escalation into a 1h-expiry KILL; a NotifierWorkflow or host supervision would make bridge death loud.
findings.notes: T3. Fold into the stack-supervision work Bryan already prioritized.

findings.summary: Escalation resolution rides signals plus store races; workflow Updates with validators would delete the race, and epic-<epic_id> fits Telegram's 64-byte callback_data.
Landing status polling emits ~11 history events/min; the D-029 heartbeat-details long-poll pattern would cut this to ~3 per landing.
findings.notes: T5. Rider on any interpreter work.

findings.summary: Epic resume after partial landings requires hand-authored remainder workgraphs (violating D-025) — no epic has ever been observed COMPLETED with all nodes MERGED across a split; start-time git reconciliation plus a retry_node signal closes it.
findings.notes: T6. Also resolves 009's continue-as-new vs child-completion tension.

findings.summary: Worker deploys mid-epic run stale code until restart (the e5c5569 landing failure); a drain-before-deploy runbook rule now, Build-ID worker versioning or workflow.patched later.
findings.notes: T7. The runbook rule is a zero-code rider; the doctor's stale-worker probe detects the condition.

findings.summary: Small Temporal-native wins: search attributes for epic/node state, the 009 preflight moved from CLI to activity, gate resume from heartbeat details.
Provider-neutral CI triggering is already the architecture: git push is the outbound trigger, polling the check rollup is the inbound path — no webhook, no public endpoint, matching D-011/D-028.
findings.notes: C1 -> ci-provider-port epic. This is the answer to the webhook question; the finding records the design so it survives as doctrine.

findings.summary: KNOWN_GATES is a closed set ('test','lint','typecheck') enforced bidirectionally at onboarding — the single blocker to richer CI; v2 needs open gate names with tier local|ci|both, an advisory flag, and structured output over the 32KiB tail.

gh.py is the one GitHub-coupled module and classify.py is already pure; a CheckProvider port (open_pr/enqueue/snapshot/dispatch/fetch_artifacts) makes AzDO pluggable — with the D-007 caveat that AzDO has no merge queue.
CI pipeline definitions should render from factory.yaml (onboard --write-ci github|azdo) so the gate set and the provider pipeline can never drift apart.
Verification splits per D-008: fast local gates (ruff, bandit, pip-audit, gitleaks) in-factory; deep CI (CodeQL/semgrep, SBOM, matrix) provider-side; the judge never in CI.

CI artifacts (SBOM, SARIF, attestations) should flow back as evidence: fetch_check_artifacts on the port, attestation bundle as git note or PR attachment; sigstore/cosign is the provider-neutral signing path vs GitHub-specific attest actions.

Agents run with --dangerously-skip-permissions and an inherited HOME — a coding agent can read ~/.config/gh and every host credential; the runtime seam exists but is dead code, and GateExecutor is the natural enforcement seam.
No secret scan runs on generated node diffs before they become PRs; gitleaks on the diff is a cheap gate that keeps an agent-pasted credential out of the repo forever.
findings.notes: F2. Rider on the bugfix or sandbox epic; also a v2 gate candidate.

findings.summary: ruff and mypy are absent from the factory's own gate set; adopting them is a constitution III amendment plus factory.yaml gates.
test.yml lacks a permissions: block and SHA-pinned actions; zizmor and Dependabot would hold the line mechanically.
findings.notes: F4. Rider; also a ci-provider-port concern.

findings.summary: The SQLite evidence stores (ledger.db, verification.db, doctor.db) have no replication; litestream gives point-in-time recovery for the factory's memory at near-zero cost.

personas.yaml is read at dispatch, so a mid-epic persona swap changes models between attempts of one epic — which actually happened 2026-08-07; snapshotting personas at epic start makes an epic's model choices an artifact.

The dev stack (Temporal dev server, worker, bridge) runs unsupervised in tmux — a five-hour undetected Temporal death has already occurred; systemd user units plus a probe-to-Telegram heartbeat are the fix, with compose'd Temporal per D-006.
findings.notes: F7. Bryan's stated trigger: soon after the in-workflow heartbeats break for the first time. Homelab change more than an epic.
